standard_prerequisites.name: The maps F and F-tilde
standard_prerequisites.statement: F sends a matching to the pair formed by its core and its two-row tableau, and F-tilde reconstructs a matching from a core and a tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two maps composed in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Stable set and restriction of a matching
standard_prerequisites.statement: The restriction of a matching to an m-invariant set of vertices is again a matching, and a matching is determined by its restrictions to a set and its complement.
standard_prerequisites.use: They let the proof reduce the comparison to the stable and the unstable part.

standard_prerequisites.name: Unstable part as a function of the tableau
standard_prerequisites.statement: The unstable chords of a matching are reconstructed from the two-row tableau through the permutation p(T).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the equation proved at the start of the argument.

core_obligations: Show that the restriction of m to the complement of its stable set equals the matching reconstructed from the tableau through p(T), using that the complement is m-invariant (source lines 987-992).
Deduce from that equation that the reconstruction F-tilde of the pair (core(m), T) agrees with m on the unstable part (source lines 994-995).
Use the well-definedness of the restriction to a set and its complement to conclude that F-tilde composed with F is the identity (source lines 992-994).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the restriction of m to the complement of the stable set with the matching reconstructed from the tableau.
Compare the two matchings on the stable and unstable parts and conclude equality.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 982-985: for a matching m in M_{N,f} with F(m) = (core(m), T), the reconstruction F-tilde of that pair returns m. The proof (source lines 986-995) does not compare the two matchings directly: it first isolates the unstable part by proving that the restriction of m to the complement of the stable set is the matching reconstructed from the tableau through the permutation p(T), a step that needs the invariance of that complement under m to make the restriction defined, and it then invokes the uniqueness of a matching with prescribed restrictions to a set and its complement. The statement records the identity of the two maps and neither the restriction equation nor the uniqueness step.
